references.text: Gabbay, Murdoch J. Aperiodic Life, version 3.7.4. Software, curated configurations and computational evidence, 14 October 2026. Catalogue: AI generated following prompts by Murdoch J. Gabbay. Editable catalogue sources and exact-state evidence accompany the release.
Edmond, James. Gliders on Aperiodic Monotilings: Cellular Automata on the Hat and Spectre. arXiv:2609.22579, 2026. Primary source for the published Hat/Spectre framework and Hat A/B/C gliders.
Edmond, James. The Glider Compendium. Author-maintained monotile-ca repository, GLIDERS.md. Rule tables, seed records and credit for reproduced behaviour.
Goucher, Adam P. Gliders in cellular automata on Penrose tilings (2012). Primary paper describing earlier four-state Penrose travelling behaviour under a different update rule.

Owens, Nick and Stepney, Susan. The Game of Life Rules on Penrose Tilings: still life and oscillators. In A. Adamatzky (ed.), Game of Life Cellular Automata, chapter 18, pp. 331-378. Springer, 2010. Author-maintained catalogue and linked chapter.

Stepney, Susan. The Art of Penrose Life. In A. Adamatzky and G. J. Martinez (eds.), Designing Beauty: The Art of Cellular Automata, pp. 103-109. Springer, 2016. DOI: 10.1007/978-3-319-27270-2_15. Figure 6 illustrates the published fireworks oscillator.
Rucker, Rudy and Walker, John. CelLab manual, rule descriptions: Brian’s Brain. Primary software documentation crediting Brian Silverman’s three-state rule.

ConwayLife forum contributors. Hexagonal Generations Rules, topic 1319. Retained dated sources include c0b0p0’s 27 February 2014 B2/S1, C=3 rotor and ship (X31, X33), and confocaloid’s 14 October 2024 B246/S246, C=4 gun (X29). Elsewhere this thread is explicitly cited as surveyed background, not evidence of an exact-rule precedent.

ConwayLife forum contributors. Outer-totalistic hexagonal rules with spaceships, topic 3670. Retained records include muzik’s 2019 B245/S35H ship (X27) and John Cerkan’s 15 March 2020 B23/S4H ship (X32). Other uses are marked as surveyed background, not exact-rule predecessors.

Owens, Nick and Stepney, Susan. Investigations of the Game of Life cellular automata rules on Penrose Tilings: lifetime, ash and oscillator statistics. Journal of Cellular Automata 5(3) (2010), 207-225.

Bays, Carter. A Note on the Game of Life in Hexagonal and Pentagonal Tessellations. Complex Systems 15(3) (2005), 245-252. Earlier hexagonal spaceships, including examples in rules B2/S35 and B245/S3.

Smith, David; Myers, Joseph Samuel; Kaplan, Craig S.; and Goodman-Strauss, Chaim. An aperiodic monotile. arXiv:2303.10798, 2023. DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2303.10798. Primary source for the Hat monotile substrate.

Gardner, Martin. The fantastic combinations of John Conway’s new solitaire game “life”. Mathematical Games, Scientific American 223 (October 1970), 120-123. Original account of Conway’s eight-neighbour, two-state rule; reproduced online.

Golly developers. QuickLife documentation: B/S notation, standard named rules and the B245/S3H hexagonal example. The H suffix denotes a hexagonal neighbourhood, specified separately in this catalogue.

ConwayLife forum discussion reached through post 28428. Retained records identify John Cerkan’s 22 January 2016 B2/S35H spaceship RLE (X23), and Dean Hickerson’s 20 January 2016 B2/S34H wall and billiard-table records (X34, X35). The link locates the discussion, not a claim that both authors wrote the linked post. Exact comparisons are retained in research/fixtures/hex-published-provenance.json.
Naszvadi. B25/S34H puffer, ConwayLife forum post, 1 February 2024. The post also notes earlier knowledge; it is evidence of prior use, not a first-discovery claim.
Eppstein, David. Replicators: HighLife. Author-maintained cellular-automaton collection; two-state B36/S23 on the eight-neighbour square grid.

Edmond, James. Interactive Hat and Spectre cellular-automaton project, offlattice.org/monotile. Companion implementation for the published rule tables and travelling behaviours described in the paper [2] and compendium [3].

Bays, Carter. A Note on the Game of Life in Hexagonal and Pentagonal Tessellations. Complex Systems 15(3) (2005), 245–252. Full text of [11]. Figure 3 describes a B2/S35 spaceship; Figure 4 describes a B245/S3 spaceship. The drawings were not independently transcribed: executable seed comparisons for X23 and X24 use Cerkan [15] and Golly [14].

drc. Pair of B2/S34H period-48 oscillators. ConwayLife forum, 18 January 2016, post 28430. One independently oscillating six-cell component is reproduced as X28; extracting that component does not make it a new oscillator.

ConwayLife forum discussion linked in the retained B25/S34H puffer provenance, reached through post 162954. Includes Dmitry Maitak’s report of an earlier occurrence. Used for the publication-history qualification in X30, not as an independently matched seed source.

ConwayLife forum post 163227 (2023), linked by Dmitry Maitak as an earlier B25/S34H puffer occurrence. Its seed has not been independently compared in this catalogue; see X30. The reported antecedent does not establish first-discovery attribution.

ConwayLife forum discussion containing Dean Hickerson’s B2/S34H self-repairing wall and period-2044 billiard-table RLEs, dated 20 January 2016 in the retained provenance. Discussion locator: post 26919. Exact seed comparisons are documented in X34 and X35.
Silver, Stephen. Life Lexicon, entries “block” and “blinker”. Golly 3.2-2 distribution retained by Debian. Pattern descriptions for S01 and S02; the blinker entry credits John H. Conway.
Silver, Stephen. Life Lexicon, entries “pentadecathlon” and “pulsar”. Golly 3.2-2 distribution retained by Debian. Pattern descriptions and Conway attribution for S04 and S03 respectively.
Silver, Stephen. Life Lexicon, entry “glider”. Golly 3.2-2 distribution retained by Debian. Credits Richard K. Guy; source for S05’s standard glider and attribution.
Silver, Stephen. Life Lexicon, entry “LWSS” (lightweight spaceship). Golly 3.2-2 distribution retained by Debian. Credits John H. Conway; source for S06.
LifeWiki contributors. “OCA:HighLife/Replicator”. Published twelve-cell B36/S23 seed used for S07. Discovery credit to Nathan Thompson (1994) is taken from Eppstein [17].
Silver, Stephen. Life Lexicon, entry “diehard”. Golly 3.2-2 distribution retained by Debian. Published seven-cell seed reproduced as S08; this catalogue does not assign an individual discoverer.

Silver, Stephen. Life Lexicon, entry “R-pentomino”. Golly 3.2-2 distribution retained by Debian. Published five-cell configuration reproduced as S09; Gardner [13] provides the contemporary account of Conway’s investigation.
Wainwright, Robert. Lifeline No. 3 (1971), p. 12. Credits the seven-cell Acorn seed to Charles L. Corderman; Wainwright supplied the name. The configuration is reproduced as S10.
Silver, Stephen. Life Lexicon, entry “acorn”. Golly 3.2-2 distribution retained by Debian. Published seed for S10; the contemporary authorship source is Wainwright [31].

Golly developers. Generations algorithm documentation. Defines the refractory-state update and lists named rule templates, including Brian’s Brain and Star Wars. This is framework documentation unless a specific named template is identified at the point of citation.

Griffeath, David, and Moore, Cristopher. Life Without Death is P-complete. Complex Systems 10 (1996), 437–447. Published study of the square-grid rule used as template U06; this citation does not identify its first inventor.

conventions.edge: Tiles share a boundary segment of positive length.
conventions.corner: Tiles touch at a boundary point but share no positive-length boundary segment. The relation key corner denotes point contact only; on the hat tiling this can include a T-junction.
conventions.touch: Edge contacts and point contacts together.
conventions.drawingCoordinates: Release renderer Float32 polygon coordinates; adjacency classifications use the exact graphs from core.js.
conventions.selection: Interior cell whose renderer centre is nearest the origin, with touch boundary distance at least 2 and at least one point-contact-only neighbour on each aperiodic tiling.
